result.title: When Credit Turns Against Tools: Transition-Aware Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains language models through multi-turn tool interactions, yet their reasoning performance and tool-calling ability can decline during training. We trace this degradation to three coupled mechanisms: (1) tool-token imbalance produces negative overall tool credit when incorrect trajectories contain more tool tokens per turn than correct ones; (2) aggregation amplification can further strengthen this negative signal as token-mean aggregation gives longer incorrect trajectories greater weight in policy updates; and (3) failure-driven retries prolong trajectories as models tend to call tools again after execution errors, extending potential negative credit to recovery attempts. To counter this suppression, we propose Transition-Aware Credit Assignment (TACA), which targets the transition from reasoning to tool use through supervision of both call initiation and generation. Specifically, TACA uses Advantage Projection to enforce a nonnegative mean advantage on tool-call tokens within each prompt group through a minimal uniform shift. Additionally, TACA guides tool-use decisions with Decision Contrast, comparing rewards for tool-assisted and direct answers to the same prompt. Through Supervised Replay, it reinforces tool-call generation using calls from previously sampled correct trajectories. Across models and tasks, TACA improves performance and sustains more reliable tool interaction during training, raising mean accuracy over MT-GRPO on six reasoning benchmarks by 4.61 percentage points for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 3.61 for Qwen2.5-3B. Our code is available at https://github.com/tmlr-group/TACA.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 agentic RL 训练中工具调用能力退化，将其归因于工具 token 不平衡、token 均值聚合放大负优势及失败重试延长轨迹，并提出 TACA，以 Advantage Projection、Decision Contrast 和 Supervised Replay 分别校正工具调用 token 优势、对比工具辅助与直接作答的收益并回放正确调用轨迹。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉多模态工作，但其对「何时调用工具」的决策对比与调用 token 的信用分配，可供核查 LVR 中 LOOK 动作的贡献分配、工具调用触发监督及推理到证据获取的过渡训练，尚未涉及 latent 内容是否被答案使用。
